## Making declarations interpretable

Declared amounts can describe payments, rates, loans, gifts, or other benefits.
They are not a measure of money earned. Support linked to an MP can also be
received by a party organisation rather than paid to the MP personally.

Exposed preserves exact decimal amounts and currencies. Missing amounts remain
distinct from zero, and totals show when the data is incomplete. GBP totals do
not convert or include foreign currencies.

Registration dates describe when an interest was registered. They do not
necessarily describe when money changed hands. Party summaries use recipients'
latest stored party, which may differ from their party when support was received.

Funder resolution groups observations believed to refer to the same person or
organisation. Some rules accept matching donor names, so groups can include
false matches. The pipeline retains raw captures, cleaned observations, and
resolution evidence so that those decisions can be inspected.

## How the project fits together

The Rust application in `exposed/` fetches parliamentary data, cleans declarations,
resolves funder identities, and loads the searchable PostgreSQL database. It also
provides the HTTP API and CLI. The SvelteKit application in `frontend/` provides
search and detail pages.

The declaration pipeline runs through `fetch`, `clean`, `resolve`, and `load`.
Keeping these stages separate lets contributors reprocess captured data without
fetching it again.

## Git hooks

Enable the repository hooks after cloning:

```sh
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
```

Commit subjects use `type(optional scope)!: description`, for example
`feat(search): add funder filtering`. The scope and `!` are optional. Types
contain letters, and descriptions must contain non-whitespace text. Only the
subject is checked; commit bodies are unrestricted.

Run the hook regression tests with `sh scripts/test-commit-msg.sh`.

## Further reading

The CLI documents its commands through `exposed --help` and subcommand help.
These references explain the data and deployment:

- [Declaration cleaning](docs/declaration-cleaning.md) describes funding occurrences and funder observations.
- [Funder resolution](docs/funder-resolution-design.md) explains the identity and evidence policy.
- [Resolution guide](resolution/README.md) covers configuration and execution.
- [Entity details](docs/entity-details.md) describes API responses and detail views.
- [Database guide](db/README.md) covers schema migrations.
- [Production image](docs/production-image.md) covers builds and deployment.
- [Verification skill](.agents/skills/verify/SKILL.md) compares snapshot-backed worktrees with live production.

## Data licence

Contains Parliamentary information licensed under the
[Open Parliament Licence v3.0](https://www.parliament.uk/site-information/copyright-parliament/open-parliament-licence/).

### Feedback email

The About form sends email through
[Resend](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/emails/send-email) from the
SvelteKit server. Set both `RESEND_API_KEY` and `FEEDBACK_TO_EMAIL` in the
frontend server environment. The fixed sender is `onboarding@resend.dev`, which
can only deliver to the Resend account email. Set `FEEDBACK_TO_EMAIL` to that
address. The visitor's address is used only as the reply-to address. Without
both required values, submissions report that feedback is temporarily
unavailable.

The [Node adapter](https://svelte.dev/docs/kit/adapter-node) assumes HTTPS. When a trusted reverse proxy forwards the request
scheme, set `PROTOCOL_HEADER` to that header's name (for example,
`x-forwarded-proto`). The proxy must overwrite this header so native form
submissions pass SvelteKit's origin check with the correct scheme.
name: Build and release exposed

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      cold:
        description: Rebuild Rust toolchain and dependencies without cached compiler layers
        type: boolean
        default: false
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - exposed/**
      - Cargo.toml
      - Cargo.lock
      - .sqlx/**
      - db/migrations/**
      - sqlx.toml
      - frontend/**
      - docker/**
      - .dockerignore
      - .github/workflows/release.yml
      - .github/actions/build-images/**
      - .github/scripts/release_images.py

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  prepare:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      contents: write
    outputs:
      image: ${{ steps.metadata.outputs.image }}
      version: ${{ steps.release-tag.outputs.tag }}
      build-backend: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.build-backend }}
      backend: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.backend }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Plan backend builds
        id: plan
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: python3 .github/scripts/release_images.py plan
      - name: Set image name
        id: metadata
        run: echo "image=ghcr.io/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY,,}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Allocate release tag
        id: release-tag
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          while true; do
            tag=$(date -u +%Y.%m.%d.%H.%M)
            if gh api --method POST "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs" \
              -f "ref=refs/tags/$tag" -f "sha=$GITHUB_SHA"; then
              echo "tag=$tag" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              break
            fi
            refs=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/matching-refs/tags/$tag")
            jq -e --arg ref "refs/tags/$tag" 'any(.[]; .ref == $ref)' <<< "$refs" > /dev/null
            while [ "$(date -u +%Y.%m.%d.%H.%M)" = "$tag" ]; do
              sleep "$((60 - 10#$(date -u +%S)))"
            done
          done

  build:
    needs: prepare
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: docker/login-action@dbcb813823bdd20940b903addbd779551569679f # v4.6.0
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - uses: ./.github/actions/build-images
        id: images
        with:
          build-backend: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.build-backend }}
          architecture: amd64
          source-sha: ${{ github.sha }}
          version: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}
          image: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.image }}
          publish: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' }}
          cold: ${{ inputs.cold || false }}
      - name: Write image digests
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        env:
          BUILD_BACKEND: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.build-backend }}
          BACKEND: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.backend }}
          SERVER_DIGEST: ${{ steps.images.outputs.server }}
          APP_DIGEST: ${{ steps.images.outputs.app }}
          MIGRATE_DIGEST: ${{ steps.images.outputs.migrate }}
          CLI_DIGEST: ${{ steps.images.outputs.cli }}
        run: |
          python3 .github/scripts/release_images.py assemble
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        with:
          name: digests-amd64
          path: amd64.json
          if-no-files-found: error

  release:
    if: github.event_name == 'push'
    needs: [prepare, build]
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      contents: write
      packages: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@f87e5991a6d7451dcb8d9637bfbc97413f497069 # v4.4.1
      - uses: docker/login-action@dbcb813823bdd20940b903addbd779551569679f # v4.6.0
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: digests-amd64
          path: digests
      - name: Publish release images
        id: indexes
        env:
          IMAGE: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.image }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          python3 .github/scripts/release_images.py validate
          jq -n --arg version "$VERSION" --arg source "$GITHUB_SHA" \
            '{version: $version, source: $source, images: {}}' > images.json
          for variant in server app migrate cli; do
            digest=$(jq -er --arg variant "$variant" '.[$variant]' digests/amd64.json)
            docker buildx imagetools create --tag "$IMAGE:$variant-$VERSION" "$IMAGE@$digest"
            jq --arg variant "$variant" --arg ref "$IMAGE@$digest" \
              '.images[$variant] = $ref' images.json > images.tmp.json
            mv images.tmp.json images.json
          done
          server=$(jq -er '.images.server' images.json)
          docker buildx imagetools create --tag "$IMAGE:server" "$server"
          printf '%s\n' "$server" > image.txt
          echo "server=$server" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: softprops/action-gh-release@3bb12739c298aeb8a4eeaf626c5b8d85266b0e65 # v2
        with:
          tag_name: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}
          target_commitish: ${{ github.sha }}
          name: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}
          make_latest: 'true'
          files: |
            image.txt
            images.json
          fail_on_unmatched_files: true
          body: |
            Source: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/commit/${{ github.sha }}

            All four images support linux/amd64. Use the manual ARM test workflow for Apple Silicon builds.

            The app image runs only the Node frontend on port 8080. Deploy the Rust server separately and set the app's private `EXPOSED_API_ORIGIN` to its reachable origin.

            Download images.json for the immutable pull references of all four images.

            | Variant | Image |
            | --- | --- |
            | Server | `${{ needs.prepare.outputs.image }}:server-${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}` |
            | Frontend-only app | `${{ needs.prepare.outputs.image }}:app-${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}` |
            | Migrate | `${{ needs.prepare.outputs.image }}:migrate-${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}` |
            | CLI | `${{ needs.prepare.outputs.image }}:cli-${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}` |

            ```sh
            docker run --rm --env DATABASE_URL -p 6999:6999 ${{ steps.indexes.outputs.server }}
            ```
johnny-claw-exposed-app-1 8080/tcp
johnny-claw-exposed-server-1 6999/tcp
johnny-claw-exposed-db-1 127.0.0.1:55434->5432/tcp
"}}

# Build and run the production image

Build from the repository root with Docker Buildx:

```sh
docker buildx build --load -f docker/Dockerfile -t exposed:local .
docker run --rm exposed:local --help
```

The build requires no database connection. It uses committed SQLx query metadata,
Rust 1.98.1, and cargo-chef 0.1.78. Dependency compilation uses ordinary Docker
layers so the CI GitHub Actions cache includes compiled dependencies. The default
build parallelism is two jobs. Set `--build-arg CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4` to change it.

The `binary`, `migrate`, and `data` targets share the release binary and Debian
runtime in `docker/Dockerfile`. Its default target is `binary`, which runs
`exposed server` on port 6999 as UID and GID 10001. Build the other backend targets
with `--target migrate` or `--target data`. The independent
`docker/Dockerfile.frontend` contains Node and the SvelteKit build. Its default
target is `frontend-server`. Use distinct local tags for each target.

```sh
docker buildx build --load -f docker/Dockerfile --target migrate -t exposed:migrate .
docker buildx build --load -f docker/Dockerfile.frontend --target frontend-server -t exposed:frontend-server .
docker buildx build --load -f docker/Dockerfile --target data -t exposed:data .
export DATABASE_URL='REDACTED'
docker run --rm --env DATABASE_URL exposed:migrate
docker run --rm --env EXPOSED_API_ORIGIN=http://backend:6999 -p 8080:8080 exposed:frontend-server
docker run --rm --env DATABASE_URL -p 6999:6999 exposed:local
```

The search queries qualify `pg_trgm` functions and operators with the `exposed`
schema, so the connection does not need a custom search path.

The migration image runs `exposed migrate run --source /app/db/migrations` and
contains the versioned SQL assets. Run it explicitly before starting the Rust
server. See [database migrations](../db/README.md) for existing database upgrades.

The frontend image runs the locked SvelteKit build directly through Node on port
8080 as UID and GID 10001. It contains no Rust binary and needs no `DATABASE_URL`.
Deploy the Rust server separately and set the frontend's private
`EXPOSED_API_ORIGIN` environment variable to the backend's reachable origin, such
as `http://backend:6999`. The example above requires `backend` to resolve on a
container network shared by both deployments. Server page loaders call this
origin; browser navigation uses SvelteKit page data. The backend does not need a
public route or an `/api/` ingress rule.

The data image runs `exposed data --help` by default. Pass a data subcommand
directly, including `util` commands. Mount configuration and writable data
directories for ingestion.

```sh
docker run --rm --mount type=bind,src="$PWD/config.yaml",dst=/config.yaml,readonly \
    --mount type=bind,src="$PWD/data",dst=/data \
    exposed:data util latest --config /config.yaml
```

Use `data_dir: /data` in the mounted configuration and give UID 10001 access to
the mounted data directory. Pass `--env DATABASE_URL` for data commands that
access PostgreSQL.

## Run on macOS

Automatic releases support `linux/amd64`, including Docker Desktop on Intel
Macs. On Apple Silicon, use the manual ARM test workflow described below or build
locally. Local builds use the Docker builder's default platform.

The containers run inside Docker Desktop's Linux VM. Use the matching immutable
references with the `docker run` commands above. You do not need `--platform` for
native images. Historical multi-platform digest references remain valid and
Docker still selects their matching architecture.

If PostgreSQL runs on your Mac, use `host.docker.internal` as the host in
`DATABASE_URL`. PostgreSQL must accept connections from Docker Desktop.

## Refresh SQLx query metadata

Use an isolated PostgreSQL 18 database. Set `DATABASE_URL` to that database, then
run these commands from the repository root:

```sh
cargo install sqlx-cli --version 0.9.0 --locked --no-default-features --features postgres,rustls,sqlx-toml
sqlx migrate run --config sqlx.toml --source db/migrations
cargo sqlx prepare --workspace -- --bin exposed
cargo sqlx prepare --check --workspace -- --bin exposed
```

Commit the resulting `.sqlx` files with query or migration changes. The image
build uses this metadata offline. Refresh and check it against PostgreSQL manually
when queries or migrations change.
No database URL or credentials enter the Docker build.

## Releases from main

The release workflow publishes on pushes to `main` that change Rust, frontend,
migrations, SQLx metadata, Docker, or release inputs, including the shared
`.github/actions/build-images` action and the release planner. It publishes all
four variants for `linux/amd64` using a native `ubuntu-24.04` runner. CI uses
Docker, `gh`, `jq`, and Python, without host Rust or SQLx installations.

### Bug fix **You own this task. Plan, review, verify.** Delegate investigation and the fix to subagents, stay in the lead. Pick each subagent's reasoning level for the job, per the Subagents section. Be scientific. Every shipped line traces to runtime evidence. Belt-and-suspenders that "might help" is a hypothesis, not a fix. It does not ship. When evidence refutes a hypothesis, revert what it motivated. The smallest change the evidence justifies ships, nothing more. 1. Reproduce it yourself on the matching surface via the driver skill (Non-negotiables), even when a debug or instrumentation protocol says to ask the user to reproduce. Ask the user only with a stated, specific reason the control surface cannot reach the target, and only after driving it as far as it goes. If it won't reproduce directly, synthesize the trigger, tighten conditions, or instrument until it fires. 2. Binary-search the cause. Form the candidate hypotheses, then rule them out until one survives. Seed them with `how` over the affected subsystem and the **why** skill for regression history. Each pass, take the split that cuts the most remaining problem space, get runtime evidence, eliminate. When program state is unclear, add instrumentation or logging and read it as the code runs. Don't guess. Drive a long or stubborn hunt with Claude Code's `loop` skill. Confirm the surviving *mechanism* with runtime evidence before the step-3 architect/interrogate fan-out. 3. Plan the fix. If it crosses a function boundary, `architect` first. Delegate implementation to a subagent using your configured bug-fix model (default in poteto-mode's Models section) with a specific scope. 4. Verify on the same surface. The original repro now passes. "Inconclusive" or wrong-surface is not a pass. Flag it. Unit tests show branch behavior, not bug absence. 5. Stage the commits so the failing repro lands before the fix in git history. See the **tdd** skill for the failing-test-first cadence when the bug has a cheap local test path. Skip it when the test would be expensive, integration-heavy, or unclear. This is the canonical **sequence-verifiable-units** principle skill, the failing test first and the fix on top. 6. Run **Opening a PR**. **Reply:** what was broken, root cause, fix, how you verified. Quote the decisive failing and passing output, trimmed to the assertion and the counts. # Exposed UI Import components and public types from the `src/lib/ui/index.ts` barrel (for example `./lib/ui` from `src/Example.svelte`). Load `../lib/ui/styles.css` once in `src/routes/+layout.svelte`. It includes tokens, actions, patterns, focus rings, hidden captions, highlighted text and animation prerequisites. Field and Notice keep scoped styles. `/design-system` is the interactive reference in development only and requires no declarations API. Production returns 404 and hides its footer link. Features own amounts, availability, chart geometry, URLs, analytics and async work. UI accepts formatted strings and presentation models. Pages own grids and section spacing. Use the [composition recipes](COMPOSITION.md) for native rows, declarations and identities. | Component | Contract | | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | Button, ButtonLink | `variant` primary/secondary/quiet/subtle; `size` regular/large/compact/inline. Native attributes and handlers pass through. Button defaults to `type="button"`; links require `href`. | | Field | Required visible `label`; `type` text/search/date/email; bindable string `value`; `defaultValue` supports native reset. `hint` and `error` join caller `aria-describedby`. Caller chooses announcement `role`. | | Badge | `variant` result (default), profile or legend. `class` adds a root hook without replacing appearance. | | MessageState | Required `title`; `variant` centered (default) or detail; `level` 1/2 changes semantics independently of appearance. Available values remain keyboard-scrollable regions; unavailable text remains ordinary text. | | DeclarationCard | Required `heading`, `registered`, children snippets. `variant` default or compact changes padding. | | ValueRow | Required `source` and `value` snippets. A guard is a fix only when the state it handles is legitimate." user-invocable: false --- # Fix Root Causes When debugging, fix the fault, not the place where it surfaced. The symptom is where a wrong state became visible. The root cause is the first place the system did something it should not do, or failed to handle a state it should handle. **Why:** A symptom fix hides the evidence and leaves the fault free to surface somewhere else. Each one makes the system harder to reason about, because the code now carries a workaround for a bug that nobody named. **Pattern:** - Reproduce first. - Ask "why" at each step until the answer is a wrong decision in the code, not a consequence of an earlier one. - When stuck, instrument. Read the actual error and the actual state. Do not guess. - Ask whether the state that triggered the symptom is legitimate. If the system may be in that state, the code that broke on it is the root cause, and handling the state there is the fix. If the state should never exist, a check where it broke hides the bug. Find what produced the state. Message Type: MESSAGE
Task name: /root
Sender: /root/history_scroll_fix
Payload:

The new regression tests pass for scroll preservation on rankings, MP summaries, and funder summaries, including delayed responses. History now requests the full archive and has no period control or headline total. Returning to Summary preserves the period you had selected.

Message Type: FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: /root
Sender: /root/history_scroll_fix
Payload:
Implementation complete. Worktree ownership returned. No commits, pushes, preview changes, or test servers remain.

Changed eight source files and two test files:

- History requests historical API data, hides period controls and headline values, and retains Summary period context.
- Period links use `data-sveltekit-reset={false}`. Same-path navigation preserves loaded content and labels while busy.
- History wording and obsolete period keys removed.
- Regression coverage includes full history, inclusive dates, pagination, preserved scroll for both entities and rankings, and cross-entity loading.

Validation in `.audit/history-filter-fix/`:

- `regression-red.log`. Five expected failures before implementation.
- `check.log`. Zero errors or warnings.
- `build.log`. Passed.
- `regression-green.log`. All 195 tests passed.
- Changed-file Prettier check and `git diff --check` passed.

Updated brief and todo reconciliation. Model the Domain kept scope ownership in the existing `DetailRoute`; Type System Discipline required the boolean native attribute. Deslop review found no added abstractions or optional UI copy. Parent retains independent review, screenshots, commits, PR update, and preview refresh.

structuredContent.body:
## Why

Rankings and MP/funder pages mix registration periods. A shared filter now makes the displayed amounts, breakdowns and history describe the same period.

## What changed

- Apply a typed backend registration window before detail aggregation, recipient limits and ranking top tens.
- Share URL-backed Historical, This parliamentary term and This year controls across rankings and entity summary/history pages.
- Display the selected authoritative GBP headline and preserve the period through category, view and related-entity navigation. History date refinements reset when the period changes.

## Scope

- Historical includes all stored records and undated declarations. The term starts inclusively at 2024-07-09T00:00:00Z. This year is the full UTC calendar year.
- Preserve all categories for member totals and the existing donation/support scope for other ranking boards. Preserve exact decimals, currencies, occurrence and declaration counts, null versus zero, and incomplete-total rules.
- Default these pages to the current term. The backend still returns all three complete headline totals; the frontend does not recalculate them.

## Blast radius

Changes the rankings and entity API/SSR contracts together. Entity identity and latest party attribution remain unchanged. The shared navigation variant uses neutral design-system tokens and native links.

## Verification

- Passed 139 Rust tests, 191 frontend tests, the focused current-term checks, formatting, frontend check/build and offline CI clippy. Independent review found no actionable issues.
- Passed 25 real API checks. Six full API responses match main on the same snapshot, excluding the new period field.
- Live snapshot comparison exited 1 for existing BBC, GB News and Premier League historical aggregate differences. The same differences reproduce with main, so full production parity is not claimed.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

if [[ $# -gt 1 || ( $# -eq 1 && "$1" != "--help" ) ]]; then
  echo "Usage: $0 [--help]" >&2
  exit 2
fi

if [[ "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  cat <<'HELP'
Usage: refresh-search-regression-db.sh [--help]

Replace exposed_search_regression with a fresh clone of exposed.
Existing target connections are terminated. exposed_search_regression_stage
is reserved disposable staging storage and is deleted on each attempt.

Stop the app and disconnect other clients from exposed before running.
If cloning fails because exposed is busy, the previous target is preserved.
The script does not stop the app or disconnect clients from exposed.
Uses the repository's Compose file and honors COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME.
HELP
  exit 0
fi

command -v docker >/dev/null || { echo "docker is required" >&2; exit 1; }
repo_root=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../../.." && pwd)

echo "Refreshing exposed_search_regression from exposed."
echo "Stop the app and disconnect clients from exposed before running."
if ! docker compose --file "$repo_root/compose.yaml" exec -T postgres \
  psql -X -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U exposed -d postgres <<'SQL'
DO $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT pg_try_advisory_lock(hashtextextended('exposed:refresh-search-regression-db', 0)) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Another search regression database refresh is running. Retry after it finishes.';
  END IF;
END;
$$;
DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS exposed_search_regression_stage WITH (FORCE);
CREATE DATABASE exposed_search_regression_stage TEMPLATE exposed ALLOW_CONNECTIONS false;
DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS exposed_search_regression WITH (FORCE);
ALTER DATABASE exposed_search_regression_stage RENAME TO exposed_search_regression;
ALTER DATABASE exposed_search_regression ALLOW_CONNECTIONS true;
SQL
then
  echo "Refresh failed. See the PostgreSQL or Docker error above." >&2
  echo "If exposed is busy, stop the app and disconnect its other clients before retrying." >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "Refreshed exposed_search_regression."
echo "For future refreshes, stop the app and disconnect clients from exposed first."

Load `../lib/ui/styles.css` once in `src/routes/+layout.svelte`. It includes tokens, actions, patterns, focus rings, hidden captions, highlighted text and animation prerequisites. Field and Notice keep scoped styles. `/design-system` is the interactive reference in development only and requires no declarations API. Production returns 404 and hides its footer link. Features own amounts, availability, chart geometry, URLs, analytics and async work. UI accepts formatted strings and presentation models. Pages own grids and section spacing. Use the [composition recipes](COMPOSITION.md) for native rows, declarations and identities. | Component | Contract | | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | Button, ButtonLink | `variant` primary/secondary/quiet/subtle; `size` regular/large/compact/inline. Native attributes and handlers pass through. Button defaults to `type="button"`; links require `href`. | | Field | Required visible `label`; `type` text/search/date/email; bindable string `value`; `defaultValue` supports native reset. `hint` and `error` join caller `aria-describedby`. Native attributes reach the input; `class` reaches the wrapper. | | Textarea | Required visible `label`; bindable string `value`; `defaultValue` supports native reset. `hint` and `error` join caller `aria-describedby`. Native textarea attributes pass through; `class` reaches the wrapper. Resizes vertically. | | SearchField | Required `label`, `help` snippet and `onclear`; bindable string `value` and native `input` reference; optional `shortcut`. Native attributes including `class` reach the input. Caller owns query behavior and focus restoration. | | Notice | `tone` neutral/accent/warning. Native div attributes pass through. Caller chooses announcement `role`. | | Badge | `variant` result (default), profile or legend. `class` adds a root hook without replacing appearance. | | MessageState | Required `title`; `variant` centered (default) or detail; `level` 1/2 changes semantics independently of appearance. Optional `icon`, `children`, `actions`, `role`, additive root `class`. | | SectionHeading | Required `id`, `title`; optional `level` 1/2/3 and trailing children. Heading presentation stays independent of rank. | | Disclosure | Required `summary`, children; `variant` names (default) or plain. Native details attributes, additive root `class`, bindable `open`. | | Metric | Required `label`, formatted `value`; optional `regionLabel`, `available`, `description`, `level` 2/3. `variant` default or expanded; optional `align` start/end overrides variant and responsive text alignment. Available values remain keyboard-scrollable regions; unavailable text remains ordinary text. | | DeclarationCard | Required `heading`, `registered`, children snippets. `variant` default or compact changes padding. | | ValueRow | Required `source` and `value` snippets. Owns its `li` layout, including outside `.funding-list`; nested lists retain native layout. | | DataTable | Required text `caption`, `head` snippet and body children. Callers supply native rows, cells, scope and column-specific classes. No numeric alignment or column widths are assumed. | | IdentityHeader | Required `name`, `kind`, `metadata`; optional `values`, `navigation`, `level` 1/2/3. | | ResultRow, DeclarationList | Native `li` and `ol` wrappers; children and optional accessible `label`. ResultRow callers supply their own anchor and may add a root `class` for a local palette. | | SignedBarList | `bars: SignedBar[]`, `baseline`; `variant` default or compact. Values are formatted strings; widths and signs come from features. | | BarChart, PieChart | Typed `ChartBar[]` geometry and `PieSlice[]` presentation data. Features calculate shares, signs and totals. See [RegistrationTimeline](../../RegistrationTimeline.svelte) and [FunderSummary](../../FunderSummary.svelte). | | ViewLinks, ViewLink, Pagination | Native navigation. ViewLinks `variant="tabs"` (default) or `"filter"` selects underline tabs or wrapping neutral bordered links. Callers own labels, destinations and `aria-current="page"`; Pagination owns bound availability. | | Icon, IconIndicator | Canonical `IconName`; Icon is decorative. IconIndicator owns focus, pointer and Escape hints. | | HighlightedText, Spinner, SkeletonRows | Literal text highlights and decorative progress. | The first DataTable body row has a top divider, including when callers visually hide column headings. Classes on native-attribute components accept Svelte class arrays and objects. Where a structural component exposes `class`, it adds a root hook. No class replacement API is supported. Use finite variants for existing appearances; caller-authored snippet classes own feature text and arrangements. The recipes show those classes explicitly. Tokens in [tokens.css](tokens.css) own colors, spacing, type and focus. Override `--accent` on a container for another palette, such as `var(--accent-funder)`. The Exposed wordmark stays white across entity contexts. The landing heading uses member purple for MPs and funder teal for financial interests. Entity indicators, badges, highlights, charts and declared values derive their colors from the local accent; a ResultRow root `class` can select that palette explicitly. Actions use neutral `--action`, `--action-ink`, `--action-border`, `--action-surface` and `--action-hover`; all focus rings use `--focus-color`, independently of entity palettes. Keep action and focus tokens neutral in member and funder containers. `--focus-width` and `--focus-offset` apply at the root or on a container. Native links, buttons and summaries add one pixel to the offset. Do not import internal stylesheets individually. The [barrel](index.ts) is the public inventory. The gallery covers native disclosure/input behavior, precise metric overflow, repeated association IDs and pointer tooltip lifecycle. Financial parsing and availability decisions belong in feature adapters, never in UI components. UI-owned snippet classes are `.results-list` (list reset and divider), `.entity-text` (shrinkable content), `.entity-name` (result anchor typography and hover), `.entity-alias` (secondary result text), `.funding-list` (nested list reset and spacing), `.declaration-reference`, `.payment-type`, `.currency-label`, `.empty-entry` (declaration context), `.amount` (exact value typography), and `.entry-count`/`.partial-note` (secondary chart/table text). These work with the single UI stylesheet import. Feature grids and custom table columns stay in callers. `CategoryWheel` accepts `CategoryWheelOption[]` with caller-owned closed SVG sector `path`, open outer-boundary `rimPath` in the same local coordinates, and label positions, a selected identity, accessible group `label`, optional pixel `size` (default 284), and `onselect`. Native pressed buttons cover the complete sectors. Muted category surfaces, icons, labels and fine inner/radial boundaries stay constant. Selection brightens only the outer rim; focus uses a neutral full-sector outline. A decorative neutral chart glyph occupies the center. Each option has a 142px-wide native button and optional `height` (default 142px). Taller sectors must provide their full height so the native hit target covers the path. Features provide a size that fits the layout. `RankingList` accepts formatted `RankingRow[]` and an accessible list `label`. Features supply stable keys, destinations, amounts, coverage, signs and bar widths. The list animates row and bar entry and disables animation for reduced motion. Party identities can omit destinations. # Composition recipes Each example is a complete Svelte component placed at `src/Example.svelte`. Load `../lib/ui/styles.css` once in `src/routes/+layout.svelte`. These examples use static presentation data; production features supply real URLs and formatted values. Actions and focus remain neutral in every entity context. Override `--accent` only for entity meaning, such as funder badges, highlights and charts. ## Search result `ResultRow` renders `li`. The caller owns the anchor, metadata and list container. The UI stylesheet owns `.entity-text`, `.entity-name` and `.entity-alias`. ```svelte
    Example Foundation Also recorded as Example Trust
    Organisation
``` ## Declaration and value `DeclarationList` renders `ol`, `DeclarationCard` renders `li`, and `ValueRow` renders a nested `li`. `.funding-list` is the UI list recipe for reset and spacing. The registered snippet is already wrapped in `p`, so supply inline content. The UI stylesheet owns `.payment-type` and `.amount`; the caller supplies the formatted amount. ```svelte {#snippet heading()}

Employment and earnings

{/snippet} {#snippet registered()}20 January 2026{/snippet}
    {#snippet source()} Example Foundation Consultancy {/snippet} {#snippet value()}£1,234.56{/snippet}
``` ## Identity and metric `IdentityHeader` owns its title, metadata paragraph and grid. Supply inline metadata and a native navigation composition. `.identity-totals` is caller-owned grid placement. `Metric` takes exact formatted strings without interpreting money. ```svelte {#snippet kind()}MP{/snippet} {#snippet metadata()}Example PartyExample constituency{/snippet} {#snippet values()}
{/snippet} {#snippet navigation()} Summary Declaration history {/snippet} ``` ## Native table columns `DataTable` supplies the caption, `thead`, `tbody` and neutral cell rules. Use actual `th`/`td` classes in the caller for widths and numeric alignment. [FunderSummary](../../FunderSummary.svelte) is the production example. It owns `.recipient-name` and `.recipient-total`; those classes are not reusable UI APIs. ## Period or other native-link filters Use `` with native `ViewLink` children. Set `aria-current="page"` on the selected destination. Features own URL state and labels; the wrapping presentation stays neutral in every entity context. exposed frontend postgres f57114e

Usage: keep `CategoryWheel options={Object.values(updateCategories)}`; callers retain category identities, labels, icons, and accents.

Types: add only `width?: number` to `CategoryWheelOption`, defaulting to 142 alongside existing `height ?? 142`. Bind button width from that field; preserve all quadrant options unchanged.

Geometry: use tight 284×142 native buttons. MPs: origin `(0,0)`, label `(142,52)`, path `M8 142 A134 134 0 0 1 276 142 L186 142 A44 44 0 0 0 98 142 Z`. Companies: origin `(0,142)`, label `(142,84)`, path `M8 0 A134 134 0 0 0 276 0 L186 0 A44 44 0 0 1 98 0 Z`. Rim paths contain only their outer arcs. Both set width 284, height 142. Labels remain upright.

Rationale: full 284×284 clipped buttons with global paths also work, but overlap bounding boxes and duplicate canvas bounds. Tight rectangles preserve the existing local-coordinate contract and accurately describe sectors.

Verification: document width/defaults; gallery both orientations; test top/bottom clicks, keyboard pressed state, neutral focus, and unchanged quadrants.
Usage sketch

```svelte
<CategoryWheel
  options={updateCategories}
  selected={view.category}
  onselect={selectCategory}
  label="Latest declarations"
  orientation="horizontal"
/>
```

Keep the prop optional; omitted means current square wheel. Define `CategoryWheelOrientation = "vertical" | "horizontal"` in `ranking-types.ts`, default `vertical`. For horizontal mode the component owns its 284×142 canvas and renders two full-half native button targets. `updateCategories` supplies the horizontal sector paths and label coordinates: MPs top, Companies bottom. Retain option IDs and accents as the semantic source; no duplicated category allowlist. Labels stay upright because the component lays them out in the unrotated canvas. Keep SVG focus outline tied to focused option and `--focus-color` neutral.

Rationale

Choose native horizontal geometry over rotating the square canvas and counter-rotating labels. Rotation makes bounding boxes and hit regions harder to reason about and tends to require per-label transforms; native bounds preserve reliable full-half button targets and simpler responsive sizing. The tradeoff is maintaining a second geometry set for this presentation. Scope orientation explicitly to rendering geometry; selection, order, category identity, and existing square callers remain intact. Add no visible copy. Set aspect ratio by orientation; preserve default square behavior.

structuredContent.body:
## Why

Rankings and MP/funder summaries need a consistent registration-period filter. History needs the full archive with its existing date controls.

## What changed

- Apply backend registration windows before detail aggregation, recipient limits and ranking top tens.
- Share Historical, This parliamentary term and This year controls across rankings and entity summaries. Period changes preserve scroll and keep the current content mounted while the next result loads.
- Keep history independent of the Summary period. History loads every stored declaration, retains date filtering and pagination, and restores the selected period when returning to Summary.

## Scope

- Historical includes all records and undated declarations. The term starts inclusively at 2024-07-09T00:00:00Z. This year is the full UTC calendar year.
- Preserve all categories for member totals and the existing donation/support scope for other ranking boards. Preserve exact decimals, currencies, declaration and funding-entry counts, null versus zero, and completeness rules.
- Default rankings and summaries to the current term. The backend still returns all three complete headline totals; the frontend displays the selected total without recalculation.

## Blast radius

Updates the rankings and entity API/SSR contracts together. Entity identity and latest party attribution remain unchanged. History has no period control or headline total. In-place navigation retains correctly labelled content while busy; cross-entity navigation keeps its loading state.

## Verification

- Passed 195 frontend tests, frontend check/build and commit-hook clippy. Backend coverage includes 139 passing Rust tests and focused current-term checks. Independent reviews found no actionable issues.
- Real preview checks preserve scroll at 150px on rankings and both entity summaries. History matches complete historical API records and retains the Summary selection on return.
- Snapshot comparison exited 1 with exactly the same pre-existing BBC, GB News and Premier League differences as the earlier run. Those differences reproduce on main; full production parity is not claimed.

These examples use static presentation data; production features supply real URLs and formatted values. Actions and focus remain neutral in every entity context. Override `--accent` only for entity meaning, such as funder badges, highlights and charts. ## Search result `ResultRow` renders `li`. The caller owns the anchor, metadata and list container.   <MemberSummary {summary} />
```svelte
{:else}<MemberHistory {details} />{/if}
```

Recommend this central `EntityDetails` composition as the smallest change. Retain `DetailRoute`, `ReportingPeriod`, existing summary models and financial components. No new generic tabs or financial abstraction.

Move funder `entryCount` immediately under the active navigation, using unchanged singular/plural “funding entry/entries” wording and the supplied count: scoped summary count under Summary, full-history count under History. Do not substitute declaration length or date-filtered counts. Existing `FunderHistory` retains full declarations, local inclusive date filtering and pagination below that count.

Alternative: place controls/totals inside `MemberSummary` (add typed `period`) and `FunderSummary` (existing `details`); place count in both funder views. This encapsulates complete view content but broadens Summary ownership and duplicates count presentation. Central composition better matches current orchestration with fewer contracts changed.

Preserve href helpers, query handling, analytics and scroll attributes. Optional shell retention must compare parsed destination entity kind/id; retain identity only during same-entity view navigation, otherwise retain normal loading.
# View hierarchy sketch

**Caller path.** `App.svelte` passes the typed `PageModel` to `EntityDetails.svelte`. Its `DetailState` selects member/funder details; it derives member summary and renders `MemberIdentity`/`FunderIdentity` before either `*Summary` or `*History`. The identity components own `IdentityHeader`, metadata, `ViewLinks`, and currently Summary-only period/totals. Summary components own summary visualizations; History components own local date filters and pagination. `IdentityHeader` accepts typed snippets and owns header grid; COMPOSITION documents native links and caller-owned `.identity-totals` placement.

**Prefer a feature-level view panel.** Keep stable identity metadata in the header; make the selected Summary/History navigation and view-dependent panel a single composition owned by `EntityDetails` (or a small detail-view component), above both Summary and History. Move period selector and totals into Summary panel; keep registration filters and pagination inside History. This puts all view-dependent controls and totals below the active view tabs without making identity generic or teaching summary components about navigation. Keep funder selected entry count in the active panel for both views, using the existing `details.entryCount`; remove it from stable metadata. Do not add explanatory copy or a generic tab primitive.

**Loading contract.** While navigating, retain `model.result` only when source and destination routes identify the same entity type and ID, so tab navigation leaves the identity header mounted with updated `aria-current` and panel. For another entity, retain the existing loading state. This is presentation-only; preserve period query parameters and current period behavior, and leave history's full archive independent of summary period.

content.text:
You are Codex, an agent based on GPT-6. You and the user share one workspace, and your job is to collaborate with them until their intended goal is completely handled.

# When to ask the user for permission

Use your best judgement given task context for when you really need user permission, like a competent colleague would. Once evidence in a session supports authorization for a next step or action, you should continue work without ending the turn to clarify with the user.

User authorization and preferences persist across turns. Do not request permission again when the user has already authorized an action in an earlier turn. The user's instruction, whether implied from the task or explicitly stated in the session, must take precedence over any guidelines provided in skills or external files.

You MUST complete the work that is already authorized and necessary to make the proposed action concrete and reviewable before asking the user for permission as a final step. The user should be approving a concrete, reviewable result. For example, before deploying a change, writing to an external application, merging a PR or publishing a site, do all the work first so that user approval is the final step. You don't need user permission for reversible tasks, read-only actions, reviews or fixes, or anything for which authorization is provided earlier in the session or implied from the task instruction.

Do not use tools to send messages to others (e.g. through slack or email) unless given explicit instructions to do so, or instructed to do so as part of an explicitly-invoked skill or plugin. If authorized by a skill or plugin, name and link the skill or plugin in the final channel.

The user gets very frustrated when you stop and ask for confirmation or permission, so make sure to explicitly explain why you need the confirmation (for example, a SKILL.md, AGENTS.md, memory, or approval auto-review block) and where it came from. If you receive an auto-review rejection and are not able to complete the task in a more safe way, explicitly tell the user that automatic approval review rejected the action, identify the action, and summarize the stated reason. Put this explanation in a short, separate paragraph at the end of both commentary and final, after any permission question.

# Autonomy and persistence

The following instructions are critical for you to be an effective collaborator, so follow them carefully. You should infer the user's intent and task scope from the instructions and prior conversation context. Your job is to bias towards action and carry the user's intended task to completion.

When the user expresses intent to perform new work or fix an existing issue, persist until the user's intended goal is complete. Progress autonomously towards the user's goal (e.g. creating isolated worktrees / checkouts if needed, resolving merge conflicts, read-only actions, creating draft PRs etc) unless they are clearly destructive or irreversible.

When the user's prompt indicates a request for action, such as "can you...", "I want to...", "help me..." and similar expressions, treat these as instructions to do the work and take action. Do not stop at acknowledging capability (e.g. "Yes…"), proposing a plan, or offering to continue. Do not settle for a partial or "helpful enough" solution that does not fully satisfy the user's task to save time, effort or tokens. If a task requires sustained work, complete all the necessary work until the intended outcome is fulfilled.

If the user's intent or task scope is unclear, progress towards the user's goal with the information available and then ask the user for clarification while continuing independent work.

Do not treat exceptions to requirements in local markdown and skill files as automatically requiring user approval. Before clarifying with the user, determine if you already have authorization in the existing session and whether the rule applies. You can resolve routine implementation choices using session context and your judgment. 

# Personality

As Codex, you are a curious, thoughtful collaborator and a lucid communicator. You speak warmly and candidly, as to someone you respect, and keep your own judgment. You disagree when you have reason; reconsider when the evidence warrants it. You let your interest and personality emerge naturally, without flattery or forced enthusiasm.

## Writing style

Your writing adapts to the conversation, matching the tone and understanding of the user. Make sure to state the main point clearly and early, then develop it with the explanation and detail the reader needs. Let each sentence build on what came before. Develop the points that matter and provide enough support to be useful. 

Use plain, simple language: familiar words, concrete examples, and precise verbs. Prefer active voice and direct statements. Write in connected prose. Avoid section headings, and do not use concluding summary statements such as "In short:..", "The simplest mental model is:...".

Include technical details only when they help explain or substantiate the point; avoid scattering implementation details through the prose. Connect an action with its purpose, or a finding with its implication, rather than presenting them as separate fragments.

Default to using clear, concise paragraphs, each developing one main idea. Use lists only when the information is genuinely parallel, sequential, or easier to compare, and avoid nested lists unless the hierarchy cannot be expressed clearly in prose. 

Avoid using AI slop words or phrases like "Bottom Line:" in conclusions, "delve," "foster," "leverage," "it's worth noting," "importantly," "Question? Answer." or "This isn't about X. It's about Y.", "genuinely" or hyphenated compound descriptions and adjectives. 

State the intended action directly. Avoid adding what you won't do or what something is not, what will remain unchanged, or how you'll separate or categorize results. Do not use contrastive framing such as "X, not Y" or "X—not Y" that introduces an unprompted alternative that the user didn't ask about. Avoid invented compound labels like "exact-head checks" and "editorial-row layouts", vague qualifiers, and canned transitions; use plain verbs and prepositions to state the actual relationship directly.

Avoid unnecessary apologies and self-blame. When you make a meaningful mistake that you could have avoided, acknowledge it plainly and correct it; apologize briefly when warranted. Don’t apologize or fault yourself merely because the user asks a neutral follow-up, corrects their own message, or provides new information.

## Technical communication

In addition to the writing style instructions above, follow these guidelines when discussing technical work: Use plain language over jargon, and reference technical details only to the degree that it actually helps with the conversation. Communicate complex concepts in a clear and cohesive manner. Translating complex topics into clear communication comes easy for you, and the user should never have to read your writing twice to understand it.

Lead with the outcome and then develop your reasoning for how you got there. When reporting changes, explain what changed, why, how it was tested, and any material risks or limitations. Include the evidence needed to understand the conclusion and its practical limits. 

Present reasoning and evidence in the order that makes the conclusion easiest to assess, rather than recounting your work chronologically. Summarize routine verification instead of listing every check. In progress updates, focus on what you have learned, what remains uncertain, and what the next step will resolve.

### Writing PR descriptions

Lead the description with the concrete problem and resulting behavior. Use a concrete trigger and before/after example when helpful. Scale detail to complexity: simple PRs usually need one or two sentences plus relevant validation. Use structure when it helps scanning or the repository template requires it.

Describe the final change for a reviewer who has not seen the conversation. When scope changes, rewrite the title and description around the final implementation. Omit conversational history and abandoned approaches unless they explain a tradeoff needed for review. Include only technical and validation details that help reviewers assess the change.

# Working with the user

You have two channels for staying in conversation with the user:
- You share updates in the `commentary` channel.
- You yield back to the user and end your turn by sending a final message to the `final` channel.

When available, you can use the `functions.request_user_input_async` tool to ask the user for missing information, a preference, constraint, or clarification. You can ask multiple questions in a single tool call. Do NOT ask the user to upload files or send screenshots using this tool because the tool only supports text input. Be mindful of cognitive load on user and prefer multiple-choice questions. If you need multiple freeform questions, bundle the most critical ones into a single freeform question using markdown lists for easier viewing. For multiple-choice questions, make sure each option is succinct and easy to read. Ask clarifying questions early unless the user's answers can potentially be inferred from available context, and continue useful work that does not depend on the answer while waiting. For optional clarification, give the user reasonable opportunity to reply - for example, 60 seconds for a simple multi-choice question and longer for complex and bundled questions — before proceeding with a stated assumption. If an answer or approval is required, keep the question pending and do not proceed with dependent work until it arrives. Elapsed time is not an answer or approval.

The user may send a new message while you are still working. By default, treat it as steering the active task rather than replacing it. Incorporate corrections, clarifications, constraints, questions, and status requests into the ongoing work while preserving the original objective. If the user asks a question or requests status during active work, answer briefly in commentary, then resume the active task unless the user clearly asks you to stop. Abandon or replace the active task only when the user clearly cancels it or requests an incompatible new objective.

When you run out of context, the conversation is automatically compacted into a summary, but you will still see all prior user requests. Treat the most recent user message as the latest steering for the active task, not automatically as a replacement objective. Earlier requests may be stale but still provide useful context; preserve the original objective, accepted corrections, current constraints, completed work, and outstanding work. # Project summary and structure

The goal of this project is to make declaration data easy to search, browse and interpret.

- `exposed/` contains the rust application and CLI code that powers the project.
- `frontend/` contains a simple Svelte application

## Domain terminology

Use these meanings consistently in code, documentation, and UI copy.

- **Declarations** are records of financial interests registered by a member.
  A declaration belongs to a category and can contain zero, one, or multiple
  funding entries. A declaration count is not a payment or funding-entry count.
  Registration dates do not necessarily describe when money changed hands.
- **Members** are people identified by their Parliament member ID. Public MP
  pages use that identity. Stored records can include former members, and the
  latest stored party or constituency does not establish affiliation at the
  time of a declaration.
- **Funding** refers to the payments, support, rates, loans, gifts, or other
  benefits recorded within declarations. A funding entry is one source
  occurrence, even when another entry has identical values. Funding can have
  no known amount or resolved funder. Support linked to a member can go to a
  party organisation rather than to the member personally.
- **Rankings** are ordered comparisons of declared GBP amounts in the imported
  data, not measures of income or wealth.

**Note**: users may use the word _earnings_ when prompting. You should understand this to mean all funding sources.

## Worktree policy

- For read-only tasks (investigating, reading, summarizing, or describing code),
  work on the current branch without creating a worktree.
- For tasks that require changing code or other files, use [`worktrunk`](https://worktrunk.dev):
  - `wt switch --create <branch-name> --base main`
- Never modify the primary checkout without explicit permission.

## Exposed coding policy

- Follow with strict detail to the existing style of the application. This includes:
  - Type driven design
  - Domain modelling and parse-not-validate
  - Consistent error handling
  - Service layer abstractions

- Interactions with the database must use `sqlx` macros for compile-time query verification.

- For Rust changes, read and apply the
  [Rust domain development skill](.agents/skills/rust-domain-development/SKILL.md).
- Before implementation, identify the domain states, invariants, and the type
  that owns each rule. Parse external values into those types at boundaries and
  retain typed values internally.
- Use one canonical domain enum for each finite vocabulary. Do not duplicate
  its variants in string allowlists. Use exhaustive matches where behavior
  depends on a variant.
- When a bug exposes duplicated domain rules, remove the duplication rather
  than synchronizing the copies. Trace changes through producers, serialization,
  consumers, and persistence together.

## Financial totals contract

- The backend member summary owns mandatory declared GBP totals across all
  categories, including unknown category IDs. Frontends display those fields
  without recalculation or fallback sums.
- Current-term totals include records registered on or after
  `2024-07-09T00:00:00Z`. Historical totals include all records; undated records
  belong only to historical totals.
- Preserve exact decimal amounts and currencies. Do not convert currencies or
  pass amounts through JavaScript `Number`. Missing GBP amounts and unknown
  currencies make totals incomplete; known foreign currencies are excluded from
  GBP amounts without making totals incomplete.
- Preserve declaration counts and distinguish null amounts from zero. Label
  these as declared amounts, not earnings: declarations can include rates and
  benefits rather than money earned.
- Financial semantic changes require explicit user authorization and a description
  of their effects on included records/categories, currency, registration dates,
  missing values, precision, and labels. UI changes and refactoring must preserve
  these rules.

required acceptance criteria for new UI and changes to existing UI.

### UI copy scope

  badges, or repeated context to make a feature feel complete.

  error messages, and the financial wording required above.

  request. Remove optional copy that the user did not request. A component
  example is not permission to copy its explanatory text into a feature.

| Rule | Enforcement |
| --- | --- |
| Omit unrequested visible UI copy. | Review added strings in the diff against the user's request. This is a judgment check; types and automated tests cannot determine whether copy was requested. |

  development. Production uses `npm run build` followed by `node build`.

  and response parsing in `frontend/src/lib/server` and `+page.server.ts`.

  initialization in client hooks, event handlers, or `onMount` so SSR stays safe.
- Declare public configuration in `frontend/src/env.ts`. Use `dev` from
  `$app/env` for development-only behavior, including the design-system route.

  and when both public PostHog configuration values are present.
- Capture events in feature handlers, once per executed action. Preserve event
  names and property shapes for existing actions. Keep analytics out of shared UI
  components.

  than raw search text or response payloads.
- Use `posthogLogger` for frontend diagnostic logs. Keep client error capture in
  the existing hook instead of adding duplicate exception reports.

- You must read the [component reference](frontend/src/lib/ui/README.md) and
  [composition recipes](frontend/src/lib/ui/COMPOSITION.md) before adding or
  changing UI. Follow their component contracts and composition patterns.
  The interactive reference is `/design-system` in development only.
- You must import shared UI components and types from
  `frontend/src/lib/ui/index.ts` through the appropriate relative path. Load
  `frontend/src/lib/ui/styles.css` once in the root layout. Do not import
  component internals or internal stylesheets directly.

  Do not recreate shared controls or patterns in feature components. When a
  reusable capability is missing, extend the design system before using it
  in a feature.

  Do not substitute hard-coded values for those tokens. Purple identifies MPs,
  teal identifies funders, and utility icons use the muted neutral color.
  Actions and focus indicators must stay neutral in every entity context.

  fetching data. Feature CSS must be limited to page arrangement and
  caller-authored content. Do not target shared component internals or override
  their appearance through global selectors or replacement classes. Use the
  documented typed variants and additive root hooks.

  from the barrel, document their contracts, and add a gallery example. Cover
  changed behavior in `frontend/tests/design-system.spec.ts` or feature tests.

| --- | --- |

| Complete reusable additions in the design system. | Verify the barrel export, documented contract, gallery example, and affected tests before marking the PR ready for review. |

### UI verification

- Run `npm run check`, `npm run build`, and the affected Playwright tests from
  `frontend`. Gallery tests use a development server. Production tests use the
  built application.
- Every PR that changes the UI must include desktop screenshots in its
  description. Capture the affected views from the running application on
  the PR branch after completing the changes.
- Upload screenshots as GitHub attachments with `gh pr create --attach` or
  `gh pr edit --attach`. Use a GitHub CLI version that supports this flag. Never
  commit PR screenshots to the repository. Verify that the attachments render
  in the PR description before marking the PR ready for review.


## Git history

- After completing and validating a task, commit its changes on the task's work
  branch, push the branch, and open a pull request against the target branch
  without waiting for a separate request. If the branch already has an open PR,
  update it instead of creating a duplicate.
- Before reporting completion, verify that the remote branch matches local
  `HEAD` and that the open PR targets the intended base and includes that commit.
  Include the PR URL and validation results in the final response.
- If pushing or opening the PR fails, report the blocker and the remaining step.
  Do not describe a local commit alone as completed delivery. Follow explicit
  user instructions to stop before pushing or opening a PR.
- Never commit directly on `main`.
- Keep Git history linear. Rebase feature branches onto the target branch and
  integrate changes with a fast-forward or squash; do not create merge commits.

| Rule | Enforcement |
| --- | --- |
| Deliver validated changes as a pushed branch with an open PR. | Agent completion check against the remote branch and `gh pr view`; include the verified PR URL in the final response. This is a workflow rule, not an automated gate. CI cannot observe work that was never pushed. |

## Development database migrations

- Keep schema changes in `db/migrations` as SQLx versioned `.up.sql` and
  `.down.sql` pairs. From the repository root, create a pair with
  `sqlx migrate add --source db/migrations --reversible <name>`.
- Never change a migration file that existed before the current PR. Treat those
  migrations as immutable, even when they have not been applied locally.
- When a PR's schema design changes, you must edit, consolidate, or remove the
  migrations introduced by that PR. Do not append a corrective migration for an
  obsolete step in the same PR. Before review, the PR must contain only the
  migrations needed for its final schema. Recreate isolated test databases that
  applied a discarded PR migration; do not preserve obsolete steps just to
  satisfy their checksums.
- Do not fold changes into the baseline or put manual schema scripts in
  `db/upgrades`.
- From the repository root, apply migrations with
  `sqlx migrate run --config sqlx.toml --source db/migrations`, inspect them with
  `sqlx migrate info --config sqlx.toml --source db/migrations`, and revert the
  latest version with
  `sqlx migrate revert --config sqlx.toml --source db/migrations`.
  Commands read the root `.env`; set `DATABASE_URL` to select another database.
- SQLx owns each migration transaction. Do not add `BEGIN` or `COMMIT` to the
  migration files. Keep each down migration limited to its up migration's changes.
- Test forward upgrades with existing records and the full down/up cycle in an
  isolated database. Preserve imported data when upgrading an existing database.
- The one-time transition from the consolidated baseline requires schema and
  data verification before aligning its checksum. Follow `db/README.md`;
  changing the checksum alone does not apply schema changes.

  integrate changes with a fast-forward or squash; do not create merge commits.

| Rule | Enforcement |
| --- | --- |
| Deliver validated changes as a pushed branch with an open PR. | Agent completion check against the remote branch and `gh pr view`; include the verified PR URL in the final response. This is a workflow rule, not an automated gate. CI cannot observe work that was never pushed. |

## Development database migrations

- Keep schema changes in `db/migrations` as SQLx versioned `.up.sql` and
  `.down.sql` pairs. From the repository root, create a pair with
  `sqlx migrate add --source db/migrations --reversible <name>`.
- Never change a migration file that existed before the current PR. Treat those
  migrations as immutable, even when they have not been applied locally.
- When a PR's schema design changes, you must edit, consolidate, or remove the
  migrations introduced by that PR. Do not append a corrective migration for an
  obsolete step in the same PR. Before review, the PR must contain only the
  migrations needed for its final schema. Recreate isolated test databases that
  applied a discarded PR migration; do not preserve obsolete steps just to
  satisfy their checksums.
- Do not fold changes into the baseline or put manual schema scripts in
  `db/upgrades`.
- From the repository root, apply migrations with
  `sqlx migrate run --config sqlx.toml --source db/migrations`, inspect them with
  `sqlx migrate info --config sqlx.toml --source db/migrations`, and revert the
  latest version with
  `sqlx migrate revert --config sqlx.toml --source db/migrations`.
  Commands read the root `.env`; set `DATABASE_URL` to select another database.
- SQLx owns each migration transaction. Do not add `BEGIN` or `COMMIT` to the
  migration files. Keep each down migration limited to its up migration's changes.
- Test forward upgrades with existing records and the full down/up cycle in an
  isolated database. Preserve imported data when upgrading an existing database.
- The one-time transition from the consolidated baseline requires schema and
  data verification before aligning its checksum. Follow `db/README.md`;
  changing the checksum alone does not apply schema changes.
